arxiv-2208-10671.title: Cardinality-Regularized Hawkes-Granger Model
arxiv-2208-10671.creator: Tsuyoshi Idé, Georgios Kollias, Dzung T. Phan, Naoki Abe
arxiv-2208-10671.description: Abstract We propose a new sparse Granger-causal learning framework for temporal event data. We focus on a specific class of point processes called the Hawkes process. We begin by pointing out that most of the existing sparse causal learning algorithms for the Hawkes process suffer from a singularity in maximum likelihood estimation.

arxiv-2208-11179.title: Celestial chiral algebras, colour-kinematics duality and integrability
arxiv-2208-11179.creator: Ricardo Monteiro
arxiv-2208-11179.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ricardo Monteiro. We study celestial chiral algebras appearing in celestial holography, using the light-cone gauge formulation of self-dual Yang-Mills theory and self-dual gravity, and explore also a deformation of the latter. The recently discussed w 1 + ∞ w_{1+\infty} algebra in self-dual gravity arises from the soft expansion of an area-preserving diffeomorphism algebra, which plays the role of the kinematic algebra in the colour-kinematics duality and the double copy relation between the self-dual theories.

arxiv-2302-00839.title: Fast Online Value-Maximizing Prediction Sets with Conformal Cost Control
arxiv-2302-00839.creator: Zhen Lin, Shubhendu Trivedi, Cao Xiao, Jimeng Sun
arxiv-2302-00839.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhen Lin, Shubhendu Trivedi, Cao Xiao, Jimeng Sun. Many real-world multi-label prediction problems involve set-valued predictions that must satisfy specific requirements dictated by downstream usage. We focus on a typical scenario where such requirements, separately encoding value and cost , compete with each other. For instance, a hospital might expect a smart diagnosis system to capture as many severe, often co-morbid, diseases as possible (the value), while maintaining strict control over incorrect predictions (the cost).

arxiv-2409-12689.title: Hysteresis Behind A Freeway Bottleneck With Location-Dependent Capacity
arxiv-2409-12689.creator: Alexander Hammerl, Ravi Seshadri, Thomas Kjær Rasmussen, Otto Anker Nielsen
arxiv-2409-12689.description: Abstract Macroscopic fundamental diagrams (MFDs) and related network traffic dynamics models have received both theoretical support and empirical validation with the emergence of new data collection technologies. However, the existence of well-defined MFD curves can only be expected for traffic networks with specific topologies and is subject to various disturbances, most importantly hysteresis phenomena.

arxiv-2411-12156.title: HNCSE: Advancing Sentence Embeddings via Hybrid Contrastive Learning with Hard Negatives
arxiv-2411-12156.creator: Wenxiao Liu, Zihong Yang, Chaozhuo Li, Zijin Hong, Jianfeng Ma, Zhiquan Liu, Litian Zhang, Feiran Huang
arxiv-2411-12156.description: Abstract Unsupervised sentence representation learning remains a critical challenge in modern natural language processing (NLP) research. Recently, contrastive learning techniques have achieved significant success in addressing this issue by effectively capturing textual semantics. Many such approaches prioritize the optimization using negative samples.

arxiv-2512-24825.title: Practising responsibility: Ethics in NLP as a hands-on course
arxiv-2512-24825.creator: Malvina Nissim, Viviana Patti, Beatrice Savoldi
arxiv-2512-24825.description: Abstract As Natural Language Processing (NLP) systems become more pervasive, integrating ethical considerations into NLP education has become essential. However, this presents inherent challenges in curriculum development: the field’s rapid evolution from both academia and industry, and the need to foster critical thinking beyond traditional technical training.

pmc-10574908.title: Development of Adaptive Point-Spread Function Estimation Method in Various Scintillation Detector Thickness for X-ray Imaging
pmc-10574908.creator: Bo Kyung Cha, Youngjin Lee, Kyuseok Kim, Alla Reznik, Oleksandr Bubon
pmc-10574908.description: An indirect conversion X-ray detector uses a scintillator that utilizes the proportionality of the intensity of incident radiation to the amount of visible light emitted. A thicker scintillator reduces the patient’s dose while decreasing the sharpness. A thin scintillator has an advantage in terms of sharpness; however, its noise component increases.

pmc-11362672.title: A central role of sulcal width in the associations of sleep duration and depression with cognition in mid to late life
pmc-11362672.creator: Caroline Faucher, Léonie Borne, Anna Behler, Bryan Paton, Joseph Giorgio, Jurgen Fripp, Renate Thienel, Michelle K Lupton, Michael Breakspear
pmc-11362672.description: Study ObjectivesEvidence suggests that poor sleep impacts cognition, brain health, and dementia risk but the nature of the association is poorly understood. This study examined how self-reported sleep duration, napping, and subjective depression symptoms are associated with the brain-cognition relationship in older adults, using sulcal width as a measure of relative brain health.

pmc-11479448.title: Curbing alcohol-associated liver disease by increasing alcohol excise taxes
pmc-11479448.creator: Feiyu Zhang, Peng Xiao, Yali Liu, Tao Liu, Yanhang Gao, Yuanyuan Ji
pmc-11479448.description: ise taxes are taxes imposed on alcoholic beverages and these taxes are typically included in the product price. Increasing the alcohol excise taxes is among the most efficient and cost-effective interventions for reducing excessive consumption of alcohol in the population.

pmc-11641504.title: Calcium Phosphate Nanoparticles as Carriers of Low and High Molecular Weight Compounds
pmc-11641504.creator: Ekaterina Popova, Victoria Tikhomirova, Assel Akhmetova, Irina Ilina, Natalia Kalinina, Michael Taliansky, Olga Kost
pmc-11641504.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Nanoparticles could improve the bioavailability of active agents of various natures to human, animal, and plant tissues. In this work, we compared two methods on the synthesis of calcium phosphate nanoparticles (CaPs), differed by the synthesis temperature, pH, and concentration of the stabilizing agent, and explored the possibilities of incorporation of a low-molecular-weight peptide analogue enalaprilat, the enzyme superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), as well as DNA and dsRNA into these particles, by coprecipitation and sorption.

pmc-11726764.title: Direct On-Chip Diagnostics of Streptococcus bovis/Streptococcus equinus Complex in Bovine Mastitis Using Bioinformatics-Driven Portable qPCR
pmc-11726764.creator: Jaewook Kim, Eiseul Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Si Hong Park, Hae-Yeong Kim, Chiara Scapoli
pmc-11726764.description: This study introduces an innovative on-site diagnostic method for rapidly detecting the Streptococcus bovis/Streptococcus equinus complex (SBSEC), crucial for livestock health and food safety. Through a comprehensive genomic analysis of 206 genomes, this study identified genetic markers that improved classification and addressed misclassifications, particularly in genomes labeled S. equinus and S. lutetiensis.

pmc-11835017.title: Pseudoalteromonas agarivorans-derived novel ulvan lyase of polysaccharide lyase family 40: Potential application of ulvan and partially hydrolyzed products in cosmetic industry
pmc-11835017.creator: Navindu Dinara Gajanayaka, Eunyoung Jo, Minthari Sakethanika Bandara, Svini Dileepa Marasinghe, Sachithra Amarin Hettiarachchi, Sithumini Wijewickrama, Gun-Hoo Park, Chulhong Oh, Youngdeuk Lee
pmc-11835017.description: Ulvan is a complex sulfated polysaccharide in the cell walls of green algae with extensive applications in food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural industries, prompting extensive studies on ulvan, its oligosaccharides, monosaccharides, and cost-effective depolymerization methods. Our primary objectives were to investigate novel ulvan-utilizing marine bacteria, perform recombinant engineering of genes responsible for ulvan depolymerization, and determine their potential industrial applications.

pmc-12598979.title: Use and reporting of intervention mapping for adaptation: a systematic review protocol
pmc-12598979.creator: Eunyoung Kang, Hugo R Sánchez-Blas, Elizabeth O Obekpa, Maria E Fernandez
pmc-12598979.description: IntroductionIntervention adaptation is likely to occur to some extent when implementing interventions in new implementation contexts. Using systematic frameworks can guide intentional and effective adaptation processes. Intervention Mapping for Adaptation (IM-ADAPT) is a framework that offers step-by-step guidance for systematic, theory-based intervention adaptation.

pmc-12749711.creator: Bo Peng, Yan Liu, Jing Qiu, Qiaoyu Zhang, Qiang Zhao, Xiayu Tian, Jing Peng, Zhiguo Zhang, Yujian Wang, Yaqin Huang, Ruihua Pang, Wei Zhou, Yuliang Qi, Yanfang Sun, Quanxiu Wang
pmc-12749711.description: NAM, ATAF1/2, and CUC2 (NAC) transcription factors are a unique family of plant proteins crucial for regulating plant biotic and abiotic stress responses. pmc-13559227.creator: Sree Kanakala, Miloš Brkljac, Matthew Banger, James Doonan, Søren Brage, Mark Blyth, Philip Rowe, Bryn Jones, Angus MacLean, Tim Lindsay
pmc-13559227.description: AimsBi-unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (Bi-UKA) is a bone-conserving, cruciate-sparing alternative to total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) do not differ between procedures. Conflicting data exist on gait preservation, and little is known about physical activity (PA) outcomes. PA is understudied in arthroplasty, despite its links with all-cause mortality.
